{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In mathematics, the '''Hasse derivative''' is a generalisation of the [[derivative]] which allows the formulation of [[Taylor's theorem]] in [[coordinate ring]]s of [[algebraic varieties]].

==Definition==
Let ''k''[''X''] be a [[polynomial ring]] over a [[Field (algebra)|field]] ''k''.  The ''r''-th Hasse derivative of ''X''<sup>''n''</sup> is

:<math>D^{(r)} X^n = \binom{n}{r} X^{n-r}, </math>

if ''n'' ≥ ''r'' and zero otherwise.<ref name=Gold28>Goldschmidt (2003) p.28</ref>  In [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] zero we have

:<math>D^{(r)} = \frac{1}{r!} \left(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}X}\right)^r \ . </math>

==Properties==
The Hasse derivative is a generalized derivation on ''k''[''X''] and extends to a generalized derivation on the [[function field of an algebraic variety|function field]] ''k''(''X''),<ref name=Gold28/> satisfying an analogue of the product rule 
:<math>D^{(r)}(fg) = \sum_{i=0}^r D^{(i)}(f) D^{(r-i)}(g)</math>
and an analogue of the chain rule.<ref name=Gold29>Goldschmidt (2003) p.29</ref> Note that the <math>D^{(r)}</math> are not themselves [[Derivation (differential algebra)|derivations]] in general, but are closely related.

A form of Taylor's theorem holds for a function ''f'' defined in terms of a [[local parameter]] ''t'' on an algebraic variety:<ref name=Gold64>Goldschmidt (2003) p.64</ref>

:<math> f = \sum_r D^{(r)}(f) \cdot t^r \ . </math>
